chapters.summary: Staff welcomes attendees, asks them to silence devices, directs testimony slips to the sergeant at arms, prohibits approaching the dais, and turns the meeting over to Chair Louis.
chapters.title: Sergeant at arms opens hearing and gives decorum instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, once again, we will be starting very shortly.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your patience.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's New York City Council hearing for the Committee on Zoning and Franchises.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we please ask that you silence all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If you would like to fill out a testimony slip, then please see one of the sergeant arms.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Approaching the front dais is strictly prohibited.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Please do not approach the front dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, you may begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Farah Louis opens the Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises, identifies herself, and lists attending council members including Farias, Shulman, Salaam, Felder, Carr, and Sanchez.
chapters.title: Chair Louis calls subcommittee to order and announces attendance

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to a meeting of the Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Farrah Lewis, Chair of the Subcommittee.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This morning we are joined by Councilmembers Farias, Shulman, Salam, Felder, Minority Leader Carr, and Jay Sanchez.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis states the subcommittee will vote on five proposals and hold three hearings, listing Fort Hamilton Mews, Park Avenue Brooklyn, 289 Kent Avenue, Sojourner Truth–Mapes, 69-67 108th Street, 108-05 68th Road, 100-12 Queens Boulevard, and South Richmond open space.
chapters.title: Chair Louis outlines five votes and three hearings on agenda

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Today we are voting on five proposals and holding three hearings.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The five proposals that we will vote on are

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Fort Hamilton Mews Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Santos-Suoso's District, Park Avenue, Brooklyn Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Ressler's District,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 289 Kent Avenue Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Ressler's District, and the Sojourner Truth MAPES Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Felice's District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And 69-67, 108th Street Rezoning, Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning, and Councilmember Shulman's District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will then hold the hearings on the following proposals.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 108-05, 68th Road Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Shulman's District, 100-12, Queens Boulevard Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Shulman's District, and South...

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Richmond Designated Open Space Amendment and Councilmember Morano's District.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis describes the hybrid format, remote registration, in-person speaker cards, live stream viewing, muting until recognized, and the two-minute limit for public witnesses.
chapters.title: Chair Louis explains hybrid public testimony procedures

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This meeting is being held in hybrid format.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public who wish to testify may testify in person or via Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public wishing to testify remotely may register by visiting the council's website at www.council.nyc.gov backslash land use to sign up.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Or for those that are in person, please see one of the sergeant at arms to prepare and submit a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public may also view live stream broadcasts of the meeting at the council's website.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you are called to testify before the subcommittee, if you are joining us remotely, you will remain muted until recognized.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: by myself to speak.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you are recognized, your microphone will be unmuted.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will limit public testimony to two minutes per witness.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis directs written testimony to the land use testimony email, requires submission within three days after the hearing closes, and asks witnesses to include the LU number or project name in the subject line.
chapters.title: Chair Louis gives written testimony submission instructions

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you have additional testimony that you would like the subcommittee to consider, or if you have written testimony, please email it to landuse at testimony.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Land use testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Written testimony must be submitted three days up to three days after the hearing is closed.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please indicate the LU number and or project name in the subject line of your email.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis requests remote witnesses remain until excused, states decorum must be observed, prohibits public speaking unless testifying, reserves the witness table, and bans video and photography at the table.
chapters.title: Chair Louis sets remote witness and decorum rules

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We request that witnesses joining us remotely remain in the meeting until excused by the chair as council members may have questions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Lastly, for everyone attending today's meeting, this is a government proceeding and decorum must be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public are asked not to speak during the meeting unless you are testifying.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who are called to testify and no video recording or photography is allowed at the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the sergeant at arms for inclusion into the record.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis introduces LUs 131 and 132 for Fort Hamilton Mews in Bay Ridge, describing 292 apartments with up to 88 affordable, zoning map and MIH actions, and recommends limiting rezoning to R7D and adding MIH option 1.
chapters.title: Chair Louis presents Fort Hamilton Mews rezoning vote and modifications

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will now proceed with the five votes.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first vote concerns LUs 131 and 132 regarding the Fort Hamilton Muse proposal and Councilmember Santos-Woslos'district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicant is seeking to develop a mixed-use residential project in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn that would have approximately 292 apartments, of which up to...

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: to 88 apartments would be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the existing residential R5B

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: and R6B districts with a C2-3 commercial overlay to a residential R7X district with a C2-4 overlay.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning tax amendment to map a mandatory inclusionary housing area.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We are recommending two modifications to this proposal.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first...

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Proposed R7X district does not provide a sufficient transaction from the lower 1-3 family homes and the four-story building behind the proposed development site along Glaston Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Therefore, we recommend that the proposed rezoning be limited to a R7D district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second modification is to add MIH option 1, which will provide the ability to include more deeply affordable apartments.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Santos also supports this project as modified, and we've been joined by Councilmember Encarnacion.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis introduces LUs 133 and 134 for Park Avenue rezoning, describing 391 apartments with up to 101 affordable, M1-1 and M1-2 to M1-4 and R6-1 changes, and recommends removing MIH option 2.
chapters.title: Chair Louis presents Park Avenue Brooklyn rezoning vote and modification

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second vote concerns LUs 133 and 134 regarding the Park Avenue rezoning proposal in Councilmember Restless District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicants consist of multiple private property owners seeking to facilitate the development of 391 apartments, community facility space, and four private schools across the city.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 10 development sites.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Among the new housing to be built, up to 101 of the apartments will be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the existing manufacturing M1-1 and M1-2 district to a new mixed-use district consisting of a pair of M1-4 district with a residential R6-1 district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning tax amendment to map a mandatory inclusionary housing area.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We are recommending one modification to remove MIH option two, which will ensure the affordable apartments are provided at lower rents affordable to families with household incomes at an average of either 40% or 60% AMI.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Restless supports this application as modified.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis introduces LUs 139 and 140 for 289 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg, describing 270 apartments with up to 83 affordable, M3-1 to M1-3A and R7X and M1-2A changes, and recommends removing MIH option 2 and adding option 3.
chapters.title: Chair Louis presents 289 Kent Avenue rezoning vote and modification

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The third vote concerns LUs 139 and 140.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Regarding 289 Kent Avenue, rezoning proposal and Councilmember Restless District applicant is seeking to develop a mixed-use residential project in Williamsburg, Brooklyn

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: that would have approximately 270 apartments, of which up to 83 units would be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the existing manufacturing M3-1 district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Partially to a mixed-use district consisting of a paired M1-3A district with a residential R7X district and a remainder to an M1-2.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 2A District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning tax amendment to map a mandatory inclusionary housing area.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We are recommending one modification to remove MIH option two and to add option three,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: which will ensure the affordable apartments are provided at lower rent affordable to families with household incomes at an average of either 40 or 60 percent AMI.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilman Baresta supports this application as modified.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis introduces LUs 135 and 136 for Sojourner Truth–Mapes in Crotona, Bronx, describing two 100% affordable buildings with 457 income-restricted apartments, R7-1 and C1-4 to R8 and C2-4 changes, and MIH mapping.
chapters.title: Chair Louis presents Sojourner Truth–Mapes rezoning vote

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The third vote concerns LUs 135 and 136 regarding the Sojourner Truth MAPES, a mixed-use rezoning proposal in Councilman Felice's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicant is seeking to develop two affordable housing buildings in the Crotona neighborhood of the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The development is proposed to be 100% affordable and would have a total of 457 income-restricted apartments.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the residential R7-1 district and C1-4 commercial overlay to a residential R8 district and C2-4 commercial overlay.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning tax amendment to map a mandatory inclusionary housing area.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Felice supports this project.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis introduces LUs 137 and 138 for 69-67 108th Street in Forest Hills, describing 59 apartments with up to 18 affordable, R1-2A to R7D and C2-4 changes, and recommends removing MIH option 2 and adding option 3.
chapters.title: Chair Louis presents 69-67 108th Street rezoning vote and modification

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The fifth and final vote concerns LUs 137 and 138 regarding the 69-67 108th Street rezoning proposal in Councilmember Shulman's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicant is seeking to develop a mixed-use residential project in Forest Hills, Queens.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That would have approximately 59 apartments with up to 18 permanently affordable apartments.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the existing residential R1-2A district to a residential R7D district with a C2-4 commercial overlay.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning text amendment to map a mandatory inclusionary housing area.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We are recommending one modification to remove MIH option 2 to add option 3,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: which will ensure the affordable apartments are provided at a lower rent, affordable to families with household incomes at an average of either 40 or 60% AMI.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Shulman supports this application as modified.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks for questions, none respond, then calls a vote to approve LUs 135 and 136 and approve with modification LUs 131 and 132, 133 and 134, 137 and 138, and 139 and 140, and asks council to call the roll.
chapters.title: Chair Louis calls vote on all five proposals and requests roll call

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, are there any members with questions or remarks at this time?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: No, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I now call for a vote to approve LUs 135 and 136 related to the Sojourner Truth MAPES rezoning proposal, to approve with modification LUs 131 and 132 related to the Fort Hamilton Muse rezoning proposal,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: LUs 133 and 134 related to the Park Avenue rezoning proposal, LUs 137 and 138 related to the 69-67

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 10th Avenue rezoning proposal, and LUs 139 and 140 related to the 289 Kent Avenue rezoning proposal.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, please call the roll.

chapters.summary: Staff calls Chair Lewis, who votes aye; Council Member Farías requests permission to explain her vote, states concerns about Sojourner Truth–Mapes union and community board negotiations, and votes aye on all.
chapters.title: Roll call begins with Chair Lewis and Council Member Farías

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair Lewis?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Furious?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Permission to explain my vote?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Permission.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I just wanted to state in terms of the Sojourner Truth MAPES rezoning

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: LU 135 and 136 application today, just in recognition of member deference and the prerogative of the council member whose district the project is located in.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I want to recognize that the community board and local union have deep concerns about the negotiation and deal made.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Those perspectives deserve to be heard and respected.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: And I hope conversations continue as the council moves towards a larger vote in the land use committee and to the stated meeting.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: My role in this committee is to consider the full land use record before us, including the proposed use, the broader needs of the community and the position of the member representing the district.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: So in this case, I'll be voting aye and supporting the request coming from Councilmember Felice.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And a larger vote aye on all.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Staff calls Council Member Shulman, who explains support for the 108th Street project and applicant promises on community space, then votes aye on all.
chapters.title: Council Member Shulman explains vote on 108th Street and votes aye on all

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilman M.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Permission to explain my vote?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So on the 108th Street project, I support it, and I also, the applicant has made promises to work with me and the community board around issues of community space and all of that, which we very much appreciate.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And with that, I vote aye on all.

chapters.summary: Staff calls Council Member Salaam, who votes aye; Council Member Felder is called; Council Member Encarnación votes aye.
chapters.title: Council Members Salaam, Felder, and Encarnación cast aye votes

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Salam.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Felder.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Inconestian?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Aye.

chapters.summary: Staff calls Council Member Sanchez, who votes aye on all items except LUs 135 and 136, for which he votes no.
chapters.title: Council Member Sanchez votes aye except on Sojourner Truth–Mapes

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Sanchez?

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Aye on all with the exceptions of LEUs 135 and 136, for which I am a no.

chapters.summary: Staff calls Minority Leader Carr, who expresses frustration about limited council negotiating authority, member deference, and the bottom 12 fast-track changes, but votes yes on Fort Hamilton Mews and the other projects.
chapters.title: Minority Leader Carr explains vote on Fort Hamilton Mews and votes yes

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Minority Leader Carr.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Permission to explain my vote.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: I just want to say a few words about the Fort Hamilton Muse project.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: You know, I listened with concern to Councilmember Santa Suoso when she spoke at the last hearing about how hamstrung she felt, given the council's increasingly limited options when it comes to negotiating land use decisions.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: You know, I represent a portion of Brooklyn just on the other side of the Verrazano Bridge from this project.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: You know, I hear from many constituents who have concerns about it.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And I think that, you know, this is just the sad place that where we've come to where a local member

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: doesn't have the institutional authority that they once had to negotiate projects on behalf of their communities, in particular at a time when Councilmember Santa Suoso is actively engaging her community about.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: The larger zoning and planning issues facing Bay Ridge.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And this project preempts that, as she articulated at the last hearing.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And I think now that we've had the publication officially of the so-called bottom 12, which is going to result in

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: fast tracking, as they call it, in a number of community districts, which is really just another way of saying selective disenfranchisement, where some members, some communities are no longer going to have the voice that they once had and that others retain.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: And I think it really shows that there's a clear legal issue that I fervently hope and believe will be explored moving forward.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: But that being said, this is the choice that we have before us, and I respect the council member in having a clear view with respect to really what is possible at this given time.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: So with that said, with great frustration, I vote yes on the Fort Hamilton Muse project, and I vote yes on the others.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you, Minority Leader.

chapters.summary: Staff reports eight affirmative votes for all items except Sojourner Truth–Mapes, and seven affirmative and one opposing for LUs 135 and 136; the vote remains open as hearings proceed.
chapters.title: Staff announces initial vote results and keeps Sojourner Truth vote open

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: So at this time, for all items announced, except for Sojourner Truth, which are LUs 135 and 136, we have eight votes in the affirmative, zero opposition, and zero abstentions.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Regarding Sojourner Truth MAPES, LUs 135 and 136, we have seven votes, affirmative one, opposing, and zero abstentions.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We're going to keep the vote open.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And proceed to the hearings.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis opens the pre-considered hearing for 108-05 68th Road in Forest Hills, describing a mixed-use residential building with about 33 apartments and eight permanently affordable units under MIH.
chapters.title: Chair Louis opens 108-05 68th Road hearing and describes proposal

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now open the hearing on pre-considered LUs regarding 108-05 68th Road, a mixed-use residential rezoning proposal in Forest Hills, Queens, and Councilmember Shulman's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The applicant is seeking to develop a mixed-use residential building that would have approximately 33 apartments.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Mandatory inclusionary housing would be mapped as part of this application, which would require that approximately eight of the apartments be permanently affordable.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis explains remote registration, in-person speaker cards, and written testimony email for the 108-05 68th Road hearing.
chapters.title: Chair Louis gives testimony instructions for 108-05 68th Road

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If anyone wishing to testify regarding this proposal,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you have not already done so, you must register online by visiting the council's website at council.nyc.gov backslash land use.

chapters.title: Council Member Shulman thanks applicant and discusses affordable housing goals

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I now recognize Councilmember Shulman for remarks.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I'd like to thank the applicant team for presenting their proposal at today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I look forward to working with them to ensure that the community's needs for affordable housing and quality public services are well served by the land use process.

chapters.summary: Shulman expands on Council Member Carr's remarks, explaining that city charter proposals voted on last year and up for a vote in November will exclude the City Council from input on certain projects, limiting future negotiations.
chapters.title: Council Member Shulman warns of reduced council input under charter changes

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I just want to expand a little bit for a second on Councilmember Carr's remarks.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: What he meant is that the city council, because of proposals that were done last year that were voted on in the city charter and that are up for

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: a vote this November, the city council will be excluded from certain projects to have any input on.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I just want folks to be aware of that so that we're trying to negotiate as much as we can, but it's going to be less and less.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I just want that to be known.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

chapters.title: Council Member Thomas-Henry explains vote and votes aye on Sojourner Truth

chapters.title: Staff announces final vote results and refers items to Land Use Committee

utterances.text: Okay, so at this time for all items discussed except Sojourner Truth, which are LUs 135 and 136, we have nine votes in the affirmative, zero opposition and zero abstentions regarding Sojourner Truth.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Again, LUs 135 and 136.

utterances.text: We have eight votes in the affirmative, one in opposition, zero abstentions.

chapters.summary: Lobel describes rezoning from R1-2A to R7A for a seven-story mixed-use community facility and residential building, with a nonprofit nursery and youth center, plus mandatory inclusionary housing at option one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: 10805 68th Road, which is block 2179, lot 1 and adjacent lot 6, would be rezoned pursuant to this application from an existing R12A zoning to an R7A zoning district,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: which at the site would facilitate a new seven-story plus cellar mixed-use community facility and residential building with roughly 38,150 square feet, of which roughly 11.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Here, penciled out at option one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide are the numbers behind the proposed development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Which as stated would be a seven-story plus cellar building at roughly a 5 FAR pursuant to R7A guidelines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide is the zoning map, which tells some of the story in terms of the existing zoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: You can see this is an R12A district, was so zoned in 2009 pursuant to the Cordmeyer Forest Hills rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Prior to that, it was an R12.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So this property has been zoned R12 or R12A since 1961.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And the community board recognized that and saw really that when you look at the area map here and the surrounding buildings, many of these buildings reflect larger floor areas than would be permitted in the R12A, which is one of the reasons I think they supported this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Immediately to the west of the site, across 108th Street, is an R71 district.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: That's a pre-existing district, so you have larger buildings along 108th to that side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: But also on our side of the street, you've got existing grandfathered or non-complying buildings as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: There's C45X and C44A zoning, allowing for R7A and R7X closer to Queens Boulevard, as well as an R8X rezoning within a block and a half of the property that was zoned in May 2025.

chapters.summary: Lobel argues the site is transit-rich near subway and LIRR, notes no residential displacement, highlights community facility needs, says Queens Community Board 6 approved the rezoning 35 to 4, and hands off to Devin Murray.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The area map, the next slide, I think tells the story well in terms of why this is a meritorious rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: 108Th Street here, a wide street per zoning at 80 feet wide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We are within 600 feet of a subway station, within half a mile of five subway lines, as well as the Long Island Railroad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So when the commission approved this, they noted the fact that this was a transit rich area, that the site itself would have no res.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: displacement indeed would allow for greater and more robust community facility uses at the site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This was also recognized by Queens Community Board 6, which notes that there's a shortage of indoor recreation space, both for nursery and pre-K kids, as well as for teenagers, which would be served by the existing site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So they were very happy to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: comply with our request and approve this rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I think the vote was 35 to 4 in favor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: It was a very strong vote.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: In addition to this, the site has good access, is on a corner lot, is within a block of Yellowstone Park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: All these things are hallmarks of what we think lead to a good rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: If you can just forward through the next several slides with photographs just to show the area of the site, as well as the surrounding six and seven story buildings, I would hand the microphone over to Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Murray, who can briefly discuss the architectural plans, and then we'd be happy to answer any questions.

utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Just to reiterate, the community board was very pleased with this application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

chapters.summary: Chair Louis notes parking is below the waiver threshold and asks how the applicant chose 12 spaces; Lobel explains the community board appreciated some parking for nonprofit pickup and drop-off and employees.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I have a few questions, and I'll hand it over to Councilmember Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Given the number, that the number of required parking spaces is below the waiver threshold, as a result, you do not have to provide parking.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: How did you determine 12 spaces was the correct number of parking spots to provide?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Could you provide more information?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll start, and if the remainder of the applicant team has any comments, they can bring those.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We have a rezoning which was approved by the subcommittee today, 6967 108th Street, as a matter of public record, a building several blocks away which did not provide parking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The community board here was happy that we were providing some parking, and it is always kind of a push and pull in terms of the availability of mass transit and the demands at the site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Here, I think the fact that there's going to be nonprofits operating here, which are going to have some pickup and drop-offs, it was useful to have some parking on the site, as well as some employees in terms of the nonprofit and the child care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So 12 spaces was a chance to bring a limited amount of cars off the street, provide some flexibility in that regard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The community board was appreciative of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: They didn't really condition the application on that, but it seemed like just a minimal number of spots we can provide, and we were happy to do it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: 69 to 67, which does have a commercial overlay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Conversations with city planning were around the fact that that project is marginally closer to Queens Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: There's a commercial overlay within a block of that property, block to two blocks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And so it was just felt to be more appropriate here to encourage residential and community facility uses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: That would be permitted under the existing zoning, rather than to bring the commercial all the way up to this site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So that was the reason, the rationale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We're happy to proceed without a commercial overlay, and I think that was appreciated by all the stakeholders as well.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis opens the pre-considered hearing for 100-12 Queens Boulevard in Forest Hills, describing a mixed-use residential building with about 389 apartments and 97 permanently affordable units under MIH.
chapters.title: Chair Louis opens 100-12 Queens Boulevard hearing and describes proposal

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now open the hearing on pre-considered LU regarding 100-12 Queens Boulevard, a mixed-use residential...

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Rezoning proposal in Forest Hills, Queens and Councilmember Shulman's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The applicant is seeking to develop a mixed-use residential building that would have approximately 389 apartments.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: While I share these concerns and continue to work with the development team to address them, I want to express my continuing support for bringing more affordable housing to Forest Hills.

chapters.summary: Ed Wallace, former council member and attorney for Benenson Capital Partners, introduces Rachel Loeb and architect Chris Fogarty, and notes early communication with Council Member Shulman.
chapters.title: Ed Wallace introduces Benenson Capital team for 100-12 Queens Boulevard

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: I was going to say good morning, but now I'm going to say good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Chairwoman Lewis, Council Member Shulman, all the members of the subcommittee, thank you for letting us speak today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: My name is Ed Wallace, and together with my partner Jay Siegel at Greenberg Traug, we're the lawyers for Benenson Capital Partners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: With me to my left is Rachel Loeb, who represents Benenson, as well as Chris Fogarty, who is the architect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: I'm particularly honored to appear before the City Council because I was once privileged to serve in this body, so it's a real treat.

chapters.summary: Wallace says Benenson has listened to the community, is close to a documented agreement with the Fontaine neighbors, and will discuss preserving retail tenants and labor union support.
chapters.title: Wallace announces agreement in principle with Fontaine and retail preservation efforts

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We have communicated with Council Member Lynn Shulman from early ULERP days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We have listened to the community, and I'm pleased to preview that we have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: I don't want to overstate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We are very close to an agreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We have an agreement in principle, and we think we'll have a documented agreement with the neighbors at the Fontaine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: They're here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: They can speak for themselves, and I don't want to put words in their mouth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: But thanks candidly to their good counsel, both the land use lawyer and another former member of the council, Dominic Rechia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We've had a very open line of communication, and I think that has served everybody well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Finally, you're going to hear more about our response to community concerns, including efforts to preserve the current retail uses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Stay together post-development with those tenants, as well as labor unions who are here to testify as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: With that, I'm going to turn it over to Rachel Loeb.

chapters.summary: Rachel Loeb explains she represents the Benenson family, which has owned the property for 70 years, and describes the intention to redevelop with more housing, affordable units, and continued retail legacy.
chapters.title: Rachel Loeb presents Benenson family history and housing goals

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: I'm Rachel Loeb.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: I represent the Benenson family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: I've worked with them for the last four years since I left EDC where I was president before this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So I'm really honored to be here sort of understanding both sides of this process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Several years ago, the Benenson family started looking at this property, which they developed and have cared for for the last 70 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: It has always been the intention at the right time to redevelop this and bring housing as the current zoning allows.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: But at that moment in time, we looked at the opportunity to bring not only more housing, but a better building to the neighborhood, as well as affordable housing, and really continue that legacy of the retail tenants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So Jay's going to walk us through the details and the architecture, and then we'll talk about the community benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So thank you.

chapters.summary: Jay Siegel describes the site on Queens Boulevard between 67th Avenue and 67th Road, current R7-1 and C1 zoning, and the requested R9X and C2 rezoning with MIH option 1.
chapters.title: Jay Siegel presents site and zoning change for 100-12 Queens Boulevard

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Thank you, Rachel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Jay Siegel, Greenberg Trauer, attorney.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: So the property is on the south side of Queens Boulevard between 67th Avenue and 67th Road.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: It occupies the entire block front.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: It is currently zoned R7-1 with a C1 overlay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: This is an application to change the zoning to R9X with a C2 overlay and to seek a MIH option 1.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: You see that the site is well suited for housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: It has a subway station right in front of it for the M&ER, and it has a bus stop as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: This is just depicting what I said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: It's currently zoned to 26,000 square foot site, currently zoned R7-1 with the C1 overlay that we're seeking to rezone to the R9X with C2.

chapters.summary: Siegel shows that as-of-right construction would be set back from streets and only about 20 feet from the Fontaine, while the proposed R9X building would have a street wall on Queens Boulevard and be set back almost 50 feet from the neighbor.
chapters.title: Siegel compares as-of-right massing with proposed R9X building

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: So on the left-hand side is the building that could be constructed under current zoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Because of sky exposure plane obligations from all three street fronts, the building to achieve the height of a little over 200 feet would have to be set back from all three streets, pushed against our real lat line, and would be a little

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: less than 20 feet from our neighbor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: What we're proposing, which is on the right-hand side in the R9X, allows a street wall building, which would be on Queens Boulevard, set back almost 50 feet from the neighbor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: And normally the purpose of sky exposure planes is to provide light and air from streets, and you can see with Queens Boulevard being about 200 feet wide here, there's not a reason to provide light near the Queens Boulevard.

chapters.summary: Siegel uses a site depiction to show the as-of-right building would be near the Fontaine's loading berth, while the proposed building would be set back nearly 50 feet.
chapters.title: Siegel details Fontaine proximity and loading berth comparison

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: This is a depiction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: You've heard a lot about the Fontaine, and we'll hear more from them directly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: But what I showed you before, in the current zoning, our building would be to the left of that loading berth area, just a little under 20 feet from the Fontaine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: This is not exactly precise, but the building I showed you would be basically in line with the blue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: garbage container against the wall, so it would be set back almost 50 feet from the building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: This just shows what I showed you before.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: So let's go to the next slide.

chapters.summary: Siegel says rezoning would increase units from 132 to 389, with about 100 affordable units, and that the proposed 215-foot height is comparable to nearby buildings like the Vista.
chapters.title: Siegel presents unit increase, affordable housing, and height context

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: This is the floor area comparisons that as a result of rezoning, there would be an increase to about 267 units from 132 to 389.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: The 132, our market rate, there's no affordable obligation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Of the 267 increase, approximately 100 would be affordable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: So while the increase is 267, the affordable increase is a significant percentage of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: And the height of the building, although it's certainly a lot longer than the Azurite building, the height is comparable to 215 feet to 209 feet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: This is a depiction of the heights of buildings in the area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: It shows us at our proposed height of 215.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: It shows that there are larger buildings just a few blocks away that were able to do something like I showed you that we could do as of right under the current zoning by setting back from different streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: The vista is 40 feet higher than us, and there are other buildings on and near Queens Boulevard that are comparable height or higher than we are.

chapters.summary: Loeb says the project responds to the housing crisis with about 100 affordable units at MIH option 1, and Benenson is committed to bringing back neighborhood-serving retail with improved spaces.
chapters.title: Rachel Loeb highlights affordable housing and retail commitments

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: And I think at this point, Rachel, it's your turn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So as we started to conceive this project and think about what the benefits would be to the community, one is creating housing, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We know we're in a housing crisis, but not only that, delivering approximately 100 affordable units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And we are proposing that we would do them at MIH1.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So really meeting the needs of the community, and that's something we heard from the community board and from the councilwoman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: As I mentioned, we developed this 70 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We've curated it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We understand our retailers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We've really always brought what we felt are the retailers that meet the moment in the community, and we are committed to that as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So we're in communication with all of our tenants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Many of them have leases that have already expired, but we really want to make sure that we bring back that neighborhood-serving retail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: It not only will benefit our neighbors, but benefit the future residents of our building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: But they'll be improved, higher ceilings, energy efficient, things like that.

chapters.summary: Loeb says the project will widen sidewalks, add street trees, exceed sustainability code as an all-electric building, include bike rooms, 38 parking spaces, EV charging, and FDNY-approved micromobility.
chapters.title: Loeb describes public realm, sustainability, and parking benefits

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: This also, with the new building, gives us an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: to widen the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: There are no street trees, put in street trees, sort of address the public realm and be a better neighbor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: I'll let Chris answer more questions, but we will be not only meeting but exceeding code around sustainability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: It'll be an all-electric building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And we really looked at, and he'll show you, contextual materials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: This came out of conversations as well with the community board.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So we've been there for 70 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We're going to be there another 70 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We want this building to feel part of the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And then finally, there will be bike rooms, electric bikes, 38 parking spaces, none are required, but having some in the basement, as well as the community board asked for EV charging

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: and FDNY approved micromobility, and so we're including that as well.

chapters.summary: Loeb notes the team listened to community board requests and incorporated them, then transitions to Chris Fogarty for design.
chapters.title: Loeb says community board requests were incorporated

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: I think we've, next slide please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, that was.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Not changed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So I just reviewed that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And finally, next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: I went through this, but we really listened and tried to incorporate the community board's requests as a result of their vote.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We can go through questions and talk more about that, but I want to make sure Chris has time to go through the design.

chapters.summary: Chris Fogarty of Fogarty Finger Architects presents a 21-story masonry building, explains use of Tudor red brick and street wall setbacks, and describes smaller retail bays, wider sidewalks, and street trees.
chapters.title: Chris Fogarty presents 21-story masonry design for 100-12 Queens Boulevard

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: My name is Chris Fogarty, Fogarty Finger Architects.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: We're very excited to present our proposal today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: We're proposing a 21-story masonry building along the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: On the south side of Queens Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: We spent a lot of time listening and hearing from the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: And we also walked the neighborhood and used some of the beautiful presidents of Tudor language of red brick and masonry and the way they play with the street wall and the height and setback.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: And we wondered how we could kind of incorporate that into our building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: So we used some of the new city of housing, city of yes housing, dormer rules and street back set rules to try and recreate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: We also pushed the building as far north as we could away from our neighbors to the south.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: And we're lucky because the sun is always casting shadows on Queens Boulevard and not on our neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: So that was a luck, not a design thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: But we're very excited to do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: And then next slide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: And then finally, we spent a lot of time thinking about how it works at the street level, as Rachel mentioned.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: We want to recreate that ability for retail of all shapes and sizes to come back, especially smaller retail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: So there's an individual smaller bays every 20 or 30 feet to allow different retail units to come.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: Again, widening the sidewalk and increasing number of street trees and working with the local community as they go through their cycling lanes and everything else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: So thank you for letting me talk.
