chapters.title: Chair Louis thanks applicant and begins questions

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Last slide.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Right on time.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks how many affordable units will have two or more bedrooms; Rachel Loeb says design is not final but the last plan had about 25 to 30 percent two- and three-bedrooms.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks about family-sized affordable units

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions, and then I'll hand it over to Councilmember Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: How many of the affordable units are expected to be family-sized apartments with two or more bedrooms?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We have not completed the design, so I can't give you the exact account, but we actually have included a significant number of twos and threes because we actually think there's a demand for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And so by the MIH rules, it will be, you know, the number of twos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So I think approximately our last plan was 25 to 30 percent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: But, you know, as we get into design, that'll get finalized.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks about the 38 accessory parking spaces; Loeb explains it is one level of self-parking in the basement alongside mechanical, storage, and bike rooms.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks how 38 parking spaces were determined

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And although parking is not required, the proposal includes 38 accessory parking spaces.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: How did you determine this amount?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So it's one level of parking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: These are currently self-parked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: There's not a, you know, manned garage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And so in the basement of our site, we need to have a variety of, you know, mechanical spaces and storage and bike rooms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And so we allocated the rest of the space to parking.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks whether the applicant considered a subway improvement density bonus; Loeb says they looked at it but not really, and Siegel says the MTA declined an easement on the site.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks about subway improvement density bonus

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And do you consider a subway improvement density bonus?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We looked at it, but not really.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We're very far from there, and we did not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Do you want to answer that?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Yeah, no, there's no...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: required us to invite the MTA to take an easement on the site, and the MTA sent us a letter declining it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: They apparently have other plans to how to make this station accessible that don't include our building.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Shulman asks whether as-of-right construction could be built right on top of the Fontaine and whether the proposal would be farther away; Siegel confirms as-of-right would be about 20 feet away and the proposal would be farther.
chapters.title: Shulman questions applicant on Fontaine and as-of-right massing

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Shulman?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I want to talk a little bit about the Fontaine.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So my understanding from your testimony is that if you would have built it as of right, in other words, you didn't have to come to the city council, you would have permission to build right on top of the Fontaine.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And that basically that under what you're proposing, you'd be farther away.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: Correct, counsel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: We couldn't be right on top.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jay Siegel
utterances.text: We'd be 20 feet away from them because they have a 19-foot, 7-inch gap between most of their building and their property line.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I'm just asking so that people know as of right what that is and what you guys are proposing.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And so, and I'm hoping that you guys come to an agreement.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Because before anybody votes on this, that has to happen.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Shulman asks about outreach to small businesses; Ed Wallace explains the tenant list, ongoing dialogue with CVS about a temporary pharmacy during construction, and efforts to help small tenants return or find replacements.
chapters.title: Shulman questions applicant on small business and CVS relocation

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Now, the small businesses, you said you've reached out to them or?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Yeah, if I can.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: I've got a full brief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: And I actually have a list of all the score footages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Go for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: The world divides into CVS and all of what I would call the smaller mom and pops.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: And I think you know it better than we know it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: There was extraordinary support for the CVS at the community board subcommittee and in our discussions even with the Fontaine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: So...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: You know, this is a business-to-business transaction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We can't sort of spill their beans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: But for CVS, which I think is primary, we have an ongoing dialogue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We're now sort of talking to them not only national, but they're focused on the possibility, possibility that they would have a temporary pharmacy nearby during construction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: I mean, let me state a sad fact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: You can't build a building without demolishing what's there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: And that's just reality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: But we are very hopeful that they will come back full swing after that and that during the construction they will at least maintain a pharmaceutical presence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: I don't want to get into trouble with them by sort of telling their story, but that's the approach we've taken.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: And in terms of the new building, we don't think that, for example, there'd be an economic barrier for that or, frankly, for the kind of retail that Benenson– you know, everybody came at us to say, well, you know, you're kicking out the–

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: no, Benenson has worked with all of these tenants, has put them there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Has made the accommodation mutually beneficial that if they want to stay after their lease expired, stay until we build.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We're not going to build probably for another year-ish, so there's time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: And then in terms of the other, each of the small ones, the question is, do you want to come back?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Let's work on that plan, and we have reached out to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: If you don't want to come back, can we replicate a similar kind of tenant so that the neighborhood doesn't feel like it lost something?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: If they want to come back, are we able to help them find a space during the course of the instruction?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Yeah, and I know that's a particular concern to you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: I will just say this, having done relocations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: The people who decide whether it's residential or commercial, where they want to be, are those people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: And the best we can do is say, stay a little longer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: Maybe here's a little, you know, idea for you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: But we are, I'm happy to say we have a client who really understands.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: They've been in the neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: So, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: And, frankly, happy to keep your office informed.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Yeah, my office will help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: And please, if you hear anything to the contrary, we want to know it.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: No, absolutely.

chapters.summary: Shulman asks how long construction will take; Loeb says full completion will take about 30 to 36 months, with the building enclosed after about two years.
chapters.title: Shulman asks about construction duration for Queens Boulevard project

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And how long will construction take?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Push the wrong button, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: This building, it will be approximately 30 to 36 months for full completion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: But once, after about two years, it's fully enclosed and they're just finishing the interiors.

chapters.summary: Shulman asks about noise, dust, and construction mitigation; Loeb says a full construction plan was negotiated with DOT and DEP, fencing agreements are recorded, and a point person will be provided.
chapters.title: Shulman asks about construction mitigation and ombudsman

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And what would you do in terms of the...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: In terms of the construction mitigation plan for the project, noise, dust, all of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Yeah, so we, there's a, it's all fully documented.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And I have to say, actually, because we were early, we went through the full EAS process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So there's a complete construction plan that's been worked out and negotiated with DOT and DEP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: And we have made some agreements around fencing that have been actually recorded against the property and other staging to minimize impact on the neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: So that's already been agreed to and recorded.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: We also said, you know, we've reached out to all of our neighbors around the block and, you know, we'll continue to have a point person who will be that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I was going to say like an ombudsman of some kind.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Because when we built on the other side of Queens Boulevard, we had some construction issues.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And so we want to make sure that there's somebody that can be contacted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Yeah, and whether it's with the owner or the contractor who we haven't picked yet, yes, that will be 100% part of the plan.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Shulman asks about flood mitigation; Chris Fogarty says new rules require retaining all roof water and releasing it slowly into the system.
chapters.title: Shulman asks about flood mitigation for large building

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And what are you doing in terms of...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: of, again, the flood mitigation and all of that because it's a huge building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: I'm going to let Chris answer that question as the architect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: My answer is similar to the last architect's, which is the new rules mean that we retain all the water, unlike today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: It's the same amount of roof, but if they don't retain it, we will.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: And then it drips back into the system over time.

chapters.summary: Shulman notes Forest Hills experiences power reductions during heat waves; Fogarty says new codes and zoning sustainability requirements will make the building's load much lower than older comparable buildings.
chapters.title: Shulman asks about all-electric building and heat wave power load

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Now, you said it'll be an all-electric building.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Just so you're aware, when we've had these heat waves, Forest Hills is one of the first ones to reduce power and content and everything else.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So how would that be mitigated?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: I can answer that too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: Because of the new codes and because of the new zoning codes, especially that help

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: with additional sustainability requirements, the load of this building would be much less than, say, a comparable building built five years ago, certainly much less than 10 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: So it's not going to be perfect, but it's going to be a lot less than it could be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: And by achieving these new standards, we're going to reduce that amount that it could have been.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: So that's not really a good answer, but it's...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: No, you know, but I just want to be mindful of that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And, you know, there's infrastructure issues and everything else.

chapters.summary: Shulman says she has been in touch with DOT about inconsistent bike lanes on Queens Boulevard, notes single-lane and express bus issues, and says coordination is needed.
chapters.title: Shulman discusses bike lane coordination with DOT

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You also, I saw in what you presented, that you said you were going to work with DOT.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: around the bike lanes because I've been in touch, we should have a conversation because I've been in touch with DOT because the previous administration, the way that the bike lanes were done was hit or miss.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And so there's no consistency of how they are done and everything else to the point where you're building this building on Queens Boulevard, it's single lane so that, and the express buses go down there.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And then if somebody is the double parks or stopped or whatever it is, they go over the barriers.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So we need to work on that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So, let me see.

chapters.summary: Shulman asks when an agreement with the Fontaine will be reached; Wallace says there is an enforceable exchange of writing with details to work out, and Shulman stresses it must happen before a council vote.
chapters.title: Shulman asks when agreement with Fontaine will be finalized

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And do you know when you'll have some agreement or think you'll have some agreement with Fontaine?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We have an exchange of writing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: It is very enforceable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: There are details to be worked out, and I think...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So before this council votes on anything...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Wallace
utterances.text: We appreciate the encouragement to accomplish that, and we'll do our utmost to do that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: That's all the questions I have.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis reminds the applicant to follow up with Council Member Shulman on the number of family-sized units, asks if colleagues have questions, and excuses the panel.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks applicant to follow up on unit count and excuses panel

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And I just want to, just a quick comment regarding the amount of units, because you didn't have an affirmative number at the time today to share with us, but I just wanted to just remind you if you could just follow up with the Council Member so that it's clear.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The amount of units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: The twos and threes?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Loeb
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That's important.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Do any of my colleagues have questions for this panel?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right, this panel is now excused.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you for being here today.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks for public witnesses; staff reports seven people in person and none online, and Chair Louis explains that witnesses will be called in panels of three with two minutes each.
chapters.title: Chair Louis calls public testimony on 100-12 Queens Boulevard

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, are there any members of the public who wish to testify remotely or in person regarding this proposal?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yes, Chair, we have seven people in person who have signed up to testify and no one online.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For members of the public here to testify, please note that witnesses will generally be called in panels of three.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you are a member of the public, sign up to testify.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please stand by when you hear your name being called and prepare to speak when I indicate that you may begin.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please also know that once all panelists in your group have completed their testimony, if remotely, you will be removed from the meeting as a group, and the next group of speakers will be meeting as a group.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Will be introduced.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Once removed, participants may continue to view the live stream broadcast of the hearing on the council's website.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public will be given up to two minutes to speak.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please do not begin until the sergeant at arms have started the clock.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The following individuals who are signed up to testify should come to the witness table now.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis calls Marilyn Solar, Lawrence Lowe, Kitty Rudiman, and Shahanaz Shalom to the witness table.
chapters.title: Chair Louis calls first public panel for Queens Boulevard

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Marilyn Solar.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Lawrence Lowe.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Kitty Rudiman.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And Shahanaz Shalom.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Shahanaz.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That's her.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Fontaine resident Shahnaz Shalom thanks sponsor Marilyn Solar, says she and her retired husband hoped to age in place, and describes fears that a 21-story building 50 feet from her windows will block light and view and worsen schools, transit, traffic, and retail access.
chapters.title: Shahnaz Shalom testifies against 100-12 Queens Boulevard impacts

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: And good afternoon, everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: My name is Shahnaz Shalom, and I live in Fountain Building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: First, I would like to thank Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Marilyn Solor, our sponsor, for negotiating with Benison Capital Partners in good faith on behalf of Fountain residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: I admire her professional.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Dedication and diligent effort to support and protect us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Hall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: I'm a UFT retiree and also my husband is retired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: We were looking forward to age in place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Unfortunately, for the past six months, we have been going through very difficult times mentally, knowing a 21-story building will be built.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: In front of us, considering our building is only six floor high.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: And this tower will be only 50 feet away from our windows, blocking our ambient light and our view permanently.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Besides, there will be more harms to our community, such as overcrowded schools,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: overburdened transportation, heavy traffic, losing businesses which provide our necessary daily needs, especially for seniors and disabled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: It is noble that city officials be responsible to provide housing for people who are in need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: But how about protecting the group of people who already have established a decent place to live?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Do they deserve to live in agony?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: I hope we

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: We, the constituents of Forest Hills, could be protected according to our needs by our elected officials as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: I appreciate your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shahnaz Shalom
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Kitty Rudiman, an 80-year-old fixed-income Fontaine resident of 17 years, says the 21-story building in front of her sixth-floor windows would leave her with no light or air and make her feel entombed.
chapters.title: Kitty Rudiman testifies about loss of light and air at Fontaine

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: My name is Kitty Rudiman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: I'm 80 years old and I'm on a fixed income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: I've been a resident of the Fontaine Gardens for the past 17 years and I've been so happy living there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: It's a lovely building and I have very lovely neighbors, but at this time we are all

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: Totally depressed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: They're planning to, I'm on the sixth floor, my windows face Queens Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: You can imagine with a 21-story high-rise right in front of my windows, I wake up in the morning and see the sky every morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: I will now have no light, no air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: I will be completely entombed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: I face homelessness, and I know no one cares, but what if it were your mother or your grandmother?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: I thank you all for your time.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Kitty.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Yeah, one second.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Lawrence Lau, a Fontaine resident and working committee member, says the rezoning would push the building away from the Fontaine compared with as-of-right, and after a town hall no resident preferred rejection; he supports the rezoning conditional on a written agreement.
chapters.title: Lawrence Lau offers conditional support if Fontaine agreement is reached

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Lawrence Lau.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: I'm a resident of the Fontaine, the building on lot one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: It's most impacted by the proposed development and would also be impacted by the rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: In addition, I am on the corporation's working committee for the development, and I am actually testifying for the rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: If there was some sort of agreement, conditional to some sort of written agreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: In short, the rezoning does allow the development to be built closer to Queens Boulevard and away from the Fontaine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: This pushes many of the quality of life issues away from our building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: And I can tell you when residents were first made aware of this development,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Many of them were very much against it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: This was in June.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Since then, as a member of the working committee, I've worked with the Fontaine board and the developers to put together some sort of massing that would be more acceptable to Fontaine residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: As it was communicated to us, what the proposed development looks like,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: It's much more favorable to residents than the as-of-right, the one proposed if the rezoning was rejected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: And last week,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Residents had a town, we held a town hall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: And I basically told them they're going to build.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: And here are some options.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Here's what it would look like if the rezoning was rejected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Here's what it would look like if the rezoning was accepted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Who wants it to be rejected?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: And nobody raised their hand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: So I think we've made tremendous progress since June.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: And I think everyone in the room would agree with me that when I say that in the next few weeks, I'd like to come to some sort of binding agreement sooner rather than later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Marilyn Solar, managing agent and board member of the Fontaine, describes the six-story 155-unit co-op, weekly negotiations with the applicant, and resident relief at a revised design; she says both sides are committed to a written agreement before the council vote.
chapters.title: Marilyn Solar describes Fontaine board's relief and path to agreement

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: My name is Marilyn Solar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: I'm the managing agent, member of board of the directors, and originally the sponsor of the Fontaine Department Owners Corp.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: The Fontaine is a six-story residential building with 155 units, originally built in the 50s as a rental property and converted to co-op in the 80s.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: Our building is adjacent to and directly behind the proposed project site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: Many of our residents, by the way, some of whom are here today, are long-time shareholders with families and or rent-stabilized stakeholders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: The applicant reached out to us over the summer, and recently we've been meeting with them weekly and engaging in direct conversation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: on how this project can move forward in a way that's acceptable to both parties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: About two weeks ago, the applicant proposed to us a design revision to potentially soften the overwhelming

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: and isolating aspect of their original plan, which when completed will be rather monolithic and run an entire city block long.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: We reviewed the applicant's revisions at the town hall meeting for residents last Monday, and I'm delighted to say that the plan was met for the most part with relief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: But more than that, it is potentially an attractive, livable, breathable compromise

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: that the board is comfortable with, and that with the proper aesthetics could be a win-win for our block and for the surrounding neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: We are relieved, as I said.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: And also grateful to everyone who worked to bring this about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: We met with the applicant again last week, and we're finally able to turn to the many logistical details that go along with such a large construction project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: Whoops.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: We're working as quickly as we can, and both sides are committed to reducing this agreement to writing before the city council vote so that the project can move forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: Based on the spirit of cooperation and goodwill that has developed over these past several weeks of working together with the applicant, we're hopeful and expect that these remaining items

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: will resolve themselves in a way that is comfortable for both sides.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: And having nothing to do with this, thank you very much for making us aware of the fast track and the disenfranchisement of your council.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: I'm glad to know that.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Shulman asks the opposing residents whether they realize rejection would allow as-of-right construction closer to the Fontaine; Kitty Rudiman says she is aware and does not know what she will do.
chapters.title: Shulman questions Fontaine residents on as-of-right alternative

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Shulman has questions.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So the...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The two of you that are against this, you do realize that if this gets rejected, that they can build as of right, elected officials have nothing to do with it, right up against the Fontaine.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You do realize that, correct?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: I am aware, and I don't know what I'm going to do.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: No, I'm just asking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: Of course I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: I've been aware.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: We've all been aware.

chapters.summary: Shulman explains that under a charter proposal, if she rejects the project the mayor and borough president could still approve it, so she is using her limited opportunity to negotiate improvements; she notes the Fontaine and stores are key issues.
chapters.title: Shulman explains charter limits and her efforts to secure agreement

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So let me just also reiterate, tell you, aside from the fast track, and I want to– I've been working with–

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: the applicant and your lawyer to make sure that this happens.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So, and that there's some kind of agreement.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: All right, that's number one.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Number two is that in a charter proposal that was voted on last November,

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: If I reject it, the mayor and the borough president can vote for it.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: and it'll still go forward.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I can use my limited opportunity to make it better.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And I want to thank the applicant has been willing to do that with me, which they don't have to, by the way.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So we're trying to do what we can.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And those are the big issues is the Fontaine and the stores, because I use those also.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You know, I live in the end pocket towers.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I go over there all the time.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The fruit store, all of them.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So we're trying to do that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: But like I said, I just want people to understand what the options are.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: They're limited at the moment.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And so we're going to try to do the best agreement that we can.

chapters.summary: Council Member Thomas-Henry asks how many shareholders abut the back of the project; Marilyn Solar describes the Fontaine's horseshoe shape and says one leg faces the new development but she has not calculated the number.

utterances.text: Are there any council members with questions?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Council member Thomas Henry.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I'm just curious, how many shareholders abut the backside of this building?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So from a view perspective and what parts of their units?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: And then on the other view, they're actually looking at the city.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Okay, but no idea approximately?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: How many of them?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: I haven't calculated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: No worries.

chapters.title: Thomas-Henry asks which rooms are obstructed at Fontaine

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I was just curious about that and what, well, the two young ladies here, like what you are on that side, what part of your unit is obstructed by this development?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The bedroom, living room?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: Everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: Everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: You're all welcome to come and visit.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: If I could estimate less than a third, because it's three towers, and then that one tower, the side of that one tower is facing, would be facing a new development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: So the other two towers would not be.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Well, all of their windows on this one side.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So those are, or they have opposite.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lawrence Lau
utterances.text: That I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marilyn Solar
utterances.text: I believe all the windows are on that side.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: My windows face Queens Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Gotcha.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kitty Rudiman
utterances.text: Kitchen, bedroom, and living room.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry

utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks if other members have questions, excuses the panel, thanks them, and calls Sarah Penneberg, Dennis Ibrick, and Shane Keats.
chapters.title: Chair Louis excuses Fontaine panel and calls next panel

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Are there any other council members with questions?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This panel is now excused.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you all for being here today and for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The next panel, we'll hear from Sarah Penneberg, Dennis Ibrick, and Shane Keats.

chapters.summary: Sarah Penenberg of SEIU Local 32BJ says the union supports responsible developers, reports Benenson's commitment to good residential building jobs with prevailing wage and benefits, and supports the project's hundreds of units including affordable housing.
chapters.title: Sarah Penenberg testifies for 32BJ support of Queens Boulevard project

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: My name is Sarah Penenberg, and I'm here today representing SEIU Local 32BJ.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: 32BJ is the largest union of property service workers in the country, representing over 175,000 members across 13 states,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: tens of thousands of commercial property service workers, security officers, and residential building staff in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: 32BJ supports responsible developers who invest in communities where they build.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: I'm happy to report that the developer of this proposed project, Beninson Capital, has made a credible commitment to the good jobs for workers who will permanently staff the building in the residential sector.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: Good jobs like these mean prevailing wage, meaningful benefits, and a pathway to the middle class for local community members who tend to fill these positions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: It's not just a job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: We need more housing to be built in every neighborhood of New York City to ensure that working families are not displaced by dwindling supply and skyrocketing rents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: The proposed development will include 398 residential units, roughly hundreds of which will be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: Restricted for low to middle income residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: As the cost of housing and living rises in New York, New Yorkers struggle to find their homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: It is important now more than ever to create affordable housing, good jobs, and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: uphold industry standards in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: For all of these reasons, 32BJ strongly supports 100-12 Queens Boulevard project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penenberg
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Denis Ibric of the New York City District Council of Carpenters supports the 100-12 Queens Boulevard proposal, citing affordable homes, revitalization above the 67th Avenue subway station, streetscape improvements, and constructive talks with Benenson about union carpentry.
chapters.title: Denis Ibric testifies for Carpenters union support

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: My name is Dennis Ibrich.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: I'm a council representative with the New York City District Council of Carpenters.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: I'm here today to express our support for the 100-12 Queens Boulevard proposal and to recognize the constructive dialogue that has taken place throughout the process.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: This is the kind of responsible development we need in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: It will bring hundreds of new homes to Forest Hills, including permanent affordable housing, while revitalizing an underutilized site directly above the 67th Avenue subway station.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: It will also bring improvements to the surrounding streetscape and new opportunities for local retail.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: For us, responsible development is also about how a project is built and make sure the people building it have the opportunity to earn good and family-sustaining careers.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: That's why I want to recognize Benison Capital for the way they have engaged with us.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: From the beginning, our conversations have been open, respectful, and productive.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: It has truly been a two-way street, and there has been real, genuine commitment to working together towards responsible union carpentry on this project.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: We've made meaningful progress, and we look forward to continuing those conversations and reaching an outcome that brings skilled union carpenters on the job.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: This is what responsible development should look like.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: Investment in the community, quality housing, and a commitment to the skilled workforce that helps make these projects possible.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: We appreciate Benison Capital's willingness to work with us, and we look forward to it.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: continuing this partnership and delivering a project that Forest Hills can be proud of.

utterances.speaker: Denis Ibric
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Shane Keats, a Queens renter, supports the rezoning, contrasts his 1994 apartment affordability with today's costs, says his carpenter daughter cannot afford to stay, and argues new apartment buildings are needed along Queens Boulevard even if beloved stores relocate during construction.
chapters.title: Shane Keats testifies as renter supporting Queens Boulevard rezoning

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: My name is Shane Keats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: I'm a renter here in Queens, and I'm here to voice my support for this rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: I moved to the city in 1994.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: Even then, apartments were expensive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: But in 1994, I got a four-to-one bedroom on $18 an hour.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: Yes, the bedroom was the size of a closet, and maybe that was a single futon at best, but I didn't need two roommates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: Fast forward to today, my daughter just put herself through carpentry school, and I thought this kid's a genius, a skilled trade that can't be replaced by a computer or AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: But this summer, she told me she's taking a job out of state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: She loves what she does.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: She loves where she lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: But as a journeyman carpenter, not union, unfortunately, she makes $25 an hour, and she can't afford to stay here and continue to build her life here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: Look, as a kid, I lived in New Jersey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: I've seen what ugly looks like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: I've seen a lot of strip malls.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: When I look at the picture of what this development is going to look like, I see Queens, not New Jersey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: And I get why some people oppose this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: And any change in a place that you love is hard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: I love my neighborhood in part because it feels like I can touch the generations that have come before me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: But I want my kid and her kid to be able to have that same experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: And along Queens Boulevard, the only way that can happen is if we let good apartment buildings go up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: single-story retail exists today, even if that means stores we love and have long relied upon have to relocate during construction, it seems a small price to pay to create new memories of cherished places for another generation of New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shane Keats
utterances.text: Thanks for considering my comments.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis thanks the panel, asks if members have questions, and excuses them.
chapters.title: Chair Louis excuses union and resident panel

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Are there any members that have questions for this panel?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Being that there are no questions, this panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you for being here.

chapters.title: Zach Miller testifies remotely in support of Queens Boulevard project

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And we also have Zach Miller online.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Zach Miller.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Fogarty
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Zach Miller.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin, Zach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Zach Miller.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: I am a longtime Forest Hills resident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: I grew up in Rego Park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: I am raising my family in Forest Hills, and I'm very supportive of this project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: I think this is the smart kind of development that the neighborhood needs to attract and maintain young families to Forest Hills to be able to also live close to relatives and friends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: While also being cognizant of transportation needs, while being cognizant of business concerns, I really do encourage this type of project, this type of forward-thinking development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: And so just as a resident, I wanted to come on and say that I am supportive of this.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Zach.
