chapters.summary: George Todorovic, Deputy Director of DCP's Staten Island office, says he managed the 2023 South Richmond Zoning Relief proposal and that this application updates designated open space rules and three specific sites.
chapters.title: George Todorovic introduces South Richmond designated open space update

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: My name is George Todorovich.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: I'm the Deputy Director of the Staten Island Borough Office at the Department of City Planning.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And I'm here with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: I'm here because I was the project manager of the South Richmond Zoning Relief Proposal that was adopted in 2023 by both the City of Planning Commission and City Council.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And this project is an update to that proposal from 2023, specifically about designated open space.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And my colleague Kari is going to explain those rules, background, and three specific sites for this project.

chapters.summary: Kari Bailey of DCP says the application seeks a zoning text amendment to modify designated open space boundaries at 181 Bayview Avenue, 381 Arbutus Avenue, and lots along Nautas Avenue, following the 2023 South Richmond Zoning Relief.
chapters.title: Kari Bailey presents purpose and three sites of DOS amendment

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: As George said, my name is Kari Bailey.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: I'm a planner at the DCB Department of City Planning Staten Island office.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And this is a public application from the New York City Department of City Planning, and we're seeking a zoning text amendment to modify designated open space, or DOS, boundaries at three sites in the South Richmond Development District.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Here you can see the three sites that are outlined here from left to right in the map.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: The first site is 181 Bayview Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: The second site is 381 Arbutus Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And the third site is a group of zoning lots along Nautas Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: This proposed text amendment is, as George said, a follow-up from Salt Richmond Zoning Relief, or CISR, from 2023, and that text amendment provided zoning relief for small properties.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And this proposed action will align with the goals of the special district by balancing development with natural feature preservation.

chapters.summary: Bailey explains DOS was created in 1975, mapped over public and private land and unimproved streets, and that private DOS requires CPC review, certification, authorization, or text amendment depending on proposed changes.
chapters.title: Kari Bailey explains history and review of designated open space

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Here's a little background in the history of Designated Open Space, or DOS.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: DOS was created in 1975 as part of the South Richmond Open Space Network.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: It was primarily mapped over public land, such as parks or DEP blue belts, but DOS was also mapped over private property, both vacant parcels and those with existing structures.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: DOS was also mapped on unimproved streets that are established on the city map, yet not included in DOT's capital plan for improvement.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And today, any privately owned zoning lot that contains DOS requires City Planning Commission review or the CPC.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And even if DOS is not being disturbed or modified, a City Planning Commission certification is required to ensure that DOS remains in its natural state.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: If there's any minor site alterations or landscaping proposed within a designated open space, then a CPC authorization is required.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: If DOS boundaries are proposed to be modified, then a text minute is required, such as this application that you see today.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And the scope of most DOS projects are limited to low-density single-family homes due to the areas in which DOS has been mapped.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Projects in DOS can range from minor site alteration

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: for rear yard amenities like pools or patios, to modest home enlargements such as kitchen additions, to new developments for one home or dozens of homes in a brand new residential community.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Todorovic says the 2023 proposal provided zoning flexibility for small properties while preserving natural features on large properties, and mostly cleaned up outdated 1975 regulations and digitized text maps.
chapters.title: Todorovic explains 2023 South Richmond Zoning Relief intent

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So, as we said, the South Richmond Zoning Relief Proposal was adopted in 2023.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: The intent of CISR, as we call it, was to provide zoning flexibility for small properties while maintaining the district goal of natural feature preservation on large properties over one acre in size.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: A majority of the proposal was cleaning up outdated zoning regulations from 1975, as Kari noted.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: As it was an update since it had not been changed since then in 50 years.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: As you can see in thumbnail number four, CISR included updates to DOS out of many other things in that proposal, digitizing the text maps, removing conflicts, things of that nature.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Next slide.

chapters.summary: Todorovic explains the 2023 methodology measured boundaries from street lines or tax blocks, digitized maps, removed conflicts with built conditions, and targeted homes built before 1975 while excluding vacant lots and large natural parcels.
chapters.title: Todorovic details DOS mapping methodology and vested homes

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So here's detailed information on the methodology from back then, updating the DOS maps, and why this application today seeks a minor follow-up to those adjustments.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: In 2023, the amendment aimed to clean up the maps from 1975 due to inconsistencies and unclear dimensions.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: For decades, this made it difficult for property owners who came to our office to determine their boundaries.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Therefore, the boundaries were measured from the nearest street line or tax block, and it was digitized using ArcGIS mapping software.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Another important update was to remove conflicts between the DOS and built conditions.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: As illustrated through the examples on the slide, you can see that over the years, several property owners have approached our office to remove these conflicts.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So the text amendment sought to pull back the boundaries where it was on top of homes, mapped on top of homes in 1975.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: This would allow for homeowners to do minor enlargements, kitchen additions, things that they shouldn't need to go for a full ULIP application for.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: It's important to note that this methodology only targeted people that homes built before 1975.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Those that were vested in the zoning.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: We did not include any vacant lots.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: The methodology did not include homes built after 1975, and it did not include large parcels of DOS that are natural for the environment.

chapters.summary: Todorovic says months after adoption, property owners reported errors, prompting DCP to fact-check; because DOS on private property was not supposed to increase, the department proposes adjusting three sites.
chapters.title: Todorovic says property owners identified mapping errors after 2023

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So, that being said, several years...

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: several months after the adoption of South Richmond Amendment, we were contacted by some property owners letting us know that they identified an error.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: This prompted our office to go back and fact check our methodology.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And that was because the mapping of DOS on private property was not supposed to increase.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And therefore, this proposed action is adjusting the boundaries on three sites, as Kari noted, and we'll just zoom into those very quickly on the next slides.

chapters.summary: Bailey says the DOS boundary at 181 Bayview Avenue would shift 60 feet north to its pre-2023 location because the 2023 amendment did not intend to increase DOS on a vacant site.
chapters.title: Kari Bailey presents Site 1 at 181 Bayview Avenue

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Kari?

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Yeah, so the first DOS site is 181 Bayview Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: It's an interior zoning lot located at the intersection of Bayview Avenue and Excelsior Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Here you can see a comparison of the existing DOS boundaries in red and the proposed, which are in green, these text maps.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: The DOS boundary would shift north to more closely align with

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: the conditions that existed before CISR that was passed in 2023 since the intent and goals of that text amendment did not contemplate increasing DOS on a vacant site.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: The DOS boundary would be moved 60 feet north to its original location before CISR.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Bailey says 381 Arbutus Avenue was a pre-1975 single-family home destroyed by fire; the proposed amendment would remove a 60-by-90-foot DOS area to allow replacement in kind.
chapters.title: Kari Bailey presents Site 2 at 381 Arbutus Avenue

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And the second site is 381 Arbutus Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: It's located a few hundred feet south of Highland Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: This zoning lot was previously improved with a single family home, which was vested and built before DOS regulations were mapped on top of this home in 1975.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: However,

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: The home has since been destroyed due to a fire and the site is currently vacant.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: So taking this site history into account, the existing DOS boundary is proposed to remove a 60 foot by 90 foot area, which is shown here in the green circle,

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: to allow for the previously existing structure to be replaced in kind.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Bailey says the Nautas Avenue DOS boundary was moved five feet closer to the street in 2023, preventing modest as-of-right enlargements for dozens of townhomes; DCP proposes resetting it to the previous location.
chapters.title: Kari Bailey presents Site 3 on Nautas Avenue

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And this is the third and last DOS site.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: It's on Nautas Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: It includes a block of existing built townhomes.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: As a result of CISR, this DOS boundary was moved five feet closer to the street, which is shown here in red.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And it removed the ability for modest as a right enlargements or expansions for dozens of homes on this block.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: So therefore, the department is proposing to reset this DOS boundary back to its previous location in green and align it with the goals of home zoning relief for small properties.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Bailey says the amendment removes outdated text from the text maps that referenced in-person maps at DCP's Staten Island office because of modern digitization and document retention changes.
chapters.title: Kari Bailey describes editorial changes to DOS text maps

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: So this proposed text amendment also includes minor editorial changes in a couple of discrete places of Article 10, Chapter 7 of the zoning resolution.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: The first is to remove outdated text from the text maps, which you can see it's X tier out here in red.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: That section references maps that are available to view in person at the Department of City Planning Staten Island Borough Office.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: But due to changes in document retention policy and modernized digitization of each map, this text no longer applies.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Bailey says section 10764 would be amended to remove references to site plan requirements, retain area plan requirements, and add a reference to an area of no disturbance in the first finding.
chapters.title: Kari Bailey explains changes to zoning resolution section 10764

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: The second editorial change is within zoning resolution section 10764, which is a city planning commission authorization for future subdivision of certain plan review sites.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: There's two instances of the section that would be amended to remove a reference to site plan requirements and retain a reference to a required area plan.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: There's also a reference to an area of no disturbance would be included to the end of this first finding that you see highlighted here in yellow.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Bailey summarizes that the amendment modifies text maps to adjust DOS boundaries at three sites, removes outdated document storage text, and clarifies submission materials and findings in section 10764.
chapters.title: Kari Bailey summarizes South Richmond DOS text amendment

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: So in summary, the New York City Department of City Planning Zoning Text Amendment is seeking to modify both text maps and zoning text.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: In Article 10, Chapter 7 of the zoning resolution, the text maps would be modified to adjust designated open space boundaries across three sites.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: and remove outdated text related to document storage and retention.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: And zoning resolution section 10764 would be modified to clarify submission requirement materials and findings.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: This concludes the presentation.

utterances.speaker: Kari Bailey
utterances.text: We're happy to answer questions.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks about consequences if corrections are not made; Todorovic says Site 1 could not build a compliant home without BSA relief, Site 2 could not replace the fire-destroyed home in kind, and Site 3 would prevent modest enlargements.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks what happens if DOS corrections are not made

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I have two good questions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And we have Councilmember Morano on the line with us as well who has questions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I understand that the text amendment mainly seeks to correct outdated or incorrect information regarding designated open spaces.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: What would happen if these corrections were not made?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: If the corrections were not made, Site 1 would not be able to build a compliant home and most likely would need to go to the BSA for relief, which would be even more onerous and against the goals of the intended 2023 plan for homeowner relief

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: to build housing.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Site 2.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Would be able to build, but not in the same footprint as the home that was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So since that home was destroyed in a fire and it did not come up in our database, since the database said there was no home, we talked with our council and they said, we can introduce this at this time to allow it to be vested so the home can be replaced in kind.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And the third site is a smaller consequence, I guess, to say, lack of a better word.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: It would prevent them from doing minor home enlargements, but it is not our intent to increase a restriction five feet into somebody's home.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: That was not the intent.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So that is a minor cleanup.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: They might still be able to do some work on the front of the house, but still, we want to correct the incorrect error we made in the 2023 proposal.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks how the corrective actions are consistent with the 2023 South Richmond Zoning Relief; Todorovic says the 2023 effort targeted pre-1975 vested homes, DCP found three missed sites out of about 700, and the fixes provide homeowner relief.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks how corrections align with 2023 South Richmond amendment

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And can you speak further as to how these corrective actions are consistent with the recently enacted South Richmond Zoning Relief Tax Amendment?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So the tax amendment from 2023 focused on homes that were built before 1975, because in 1975, any home that existed had

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: this DOS rule mapped upon it.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And for the past 50 years, I've only been there 10 years, but 40 before me and 10 while I've been there, our office has been asked, why do I have this map on my site?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And we said, well, you know, now we have GIS, now we have softwares to accurately map this, so we will clean this up.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And we got very close.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And there's three sites that we missed.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: We, Kari sent a flyer with a QR code to the community board.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: We sent an interactive map.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: We said, this is the last time.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: We're going to do this one more time to clean it up.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And we found three sites out of, I think, 700.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So I think it's pretty good, but, you know, not perfect.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And that's why we're fixing these last three.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And the connection to 1975, again, is to help all the vested homes that were already existing that said, why is this happening to me?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And to provide homeowner relief for modest home improvement and home construction.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

chapters.summary: Council Member Morano introduces himself, says the application is largely corrective, and asks whether any property would gain qualifying site status; Todorovic says none are qualifying residential sites and they cannot obtain zoning bonuses or relief.
chapters.title: Morano asks whether amendment creates qualifying site status

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilman Murano.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Hello, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, everybody.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you for the presentation.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair, for your leadership of this committee.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember, do you have questions for this panel?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So, you know, for people that don't know, I'm Councilmember Frank Morano, and this application involves properties within my district in the special South Richmond Development District.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as I understand it, the purpose of this amendment, as the folks mentioned, is largely corrective.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It seeks to address mapping and record-keeping discrepancies involving designated open space.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I'm generally supportive of correcting errors that have created unnecessary complications for homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But I also want to make sure that a technical correction doesn't unintentionally create new development rights or other consequences that were never intended.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So the community board raised concerns that some properties could potentially be treated as qualifying sites under this proposal.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Can you explain whether this amendment would cause any property to obtain qualifying site status that it doesn't have today?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And if so, what additional development rights would come with that designation?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: That's a great question.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And to your point, we did discuss this with the community.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: We do have to admit that during referral,

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: There was some confusion, and we did clean that up after the community board referral was submitted.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So you might see...

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: A little discrepancy in the community board's referral based on incorrect information we had provided.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: But after confirming with our zoning division and also with our other internal divisions, none of these sites are qualifying residential sites.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: They cannot obtain any zoning bonuses or zoning relief from the qualifying residential site text.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: This would simply allow for the DOS area to be carved out, the 60 feet dimension for site one that Kari noted, the 50 by 90 foot

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: volume that Kari noted for site two, and the five foot, the small five foot dimension for site three.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And that would just allow the reorientation of the building.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: No additional FAR, no additional typologies or height.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So these sites are not QRS.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: To be QRS, they would need to be on a wide street.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: You can ask DOT whether or not they're going to widen the street, but that is something outside of this application.

chapters.summary: Morano asks whether the amendment increases floor area, height, density, dwelling units, or other zoning benefits; Todorovic says no, it only allows lateral reorientation under the same lot coverage, height, and FAR.
chapters.title: Morano asks whether amendment increases development potential

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And a lot of my constituents are concerned about some of the new zoning rules, and we don't have to get into the merits of City of Yes or the Fast Track or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But I can tell you there's a lot of concern about what that may mean for development in our community.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And so relatedly, I want to be very clear on...

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: development potential.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Would this amendment increase what can be built on any affected property, whether through additional floor area, greater height, increased density, additional dwelling units, or any other zoning benefit?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: No, no increased density, no increased height.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: It would simply allow for the reorientation of buildings because now the property owner has more space to work with, but they're still limited to the same lock coverage, the same height restrictions, the same FAR.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: None of those change.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: It's more of a lateral correction that we're doing to provide flexibility, not anything due to volume or intensity.

chapters.summary: Morano asks whether the proposed single-family home at 181 Bayview Avenue is consistent with R3X zoning and whether the amendment is necessary; Todorovic says it is consistent and necessary because the lot would otherwise be too narrow and might need BSA relief.
chapters.title: Morano asks about 181 Bayview Avenue home and necessity of amendment

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: With respect to 181 Bayview Avenue, the materials indicate that the property owner is separately seeking a zoning certification to facilitate construction of a new single-family home.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Is the proposed home otherwise consistent with the existing R3X zoning, and is this amendment necessary to allow that home to be built?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Yes, it is consistent and it is necessary because if we did not pursue this tax amendment, the property would be, correct me if I'm wrong, like 20 feet wide.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: They wouldn't be able to comply with yards.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: It would be extremely narrow, funny looking house, and they may need to go to the BSA for additional relief.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So this was actually the site that first informed us.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: of the change in the map.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And we acknowledge that this is something that we did not intend in 2023, wholeheartedly did not intend.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: This was not supposed to happen, so we are correcting it.

chapters.summary: Morano asks whether environmental review identified impacts on wetlands, trees, open space, or drainage; Todorovic says no specific impacts were identified because DOS changes were on disturbed areas, and remaining DOS areas with sensitive features were kept.
chapters.title: Morano asks about environmental review and sensitive resources

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Has the environmental review identified any potential impact on wetlands, trees, natural features, open space, drainage, or other environmentally sensitive resources?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And if so, what protections or mitigation measures are being required?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: I don't know the specifics of the, I don't know any specific impacts that may have been identified.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: There weren't any, I don't know any potential ones, but I will say that based on the methodology at a comprehensive level, there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Any specific impacts because most of the DOS changes were already on disturbed areas, such as overtop building footprints.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Again, if a home was built in 1975 and DOS was on top of it, that doesn't really align.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So we removed it.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Any DOS area that does remain does have sensitive natural features.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So there may be some adjacencies or buffers, but we kept it in the places that do have wetlands, that do have trees.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So again, we could look to the specifics of the actual document, but the DOS was moved where it was on top of existing structures or on top of other structures such as we saw.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Some basketball courts, gazebos, and swimming pools in people's backyards.

chapters.summary: Morano begins asking about environmental protections; Catie Ferrara Iannitto adds that DOS is a zoning regulation, not an environmental regulation, and wetlands, parkland, and other protections remain in place through other agencies.
chapters.title: Morano asks about environmental protections; Ferrara clarifies DOS is zoning regulation

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I also want to ask about the, sorry.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Katie, do you have a follow-up?

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: I just want to add a little further context to George's response.

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: Katie Farrar, IANIDO Director of DCP Staten Island Office.

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: We just note that DOS itself is a zoning regulation.

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: I would not define it as an environmental regulation.

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: So there are still layers of regulatory protection on any existing wetlands by Department of Environmental Conservation, other agencies.

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: Parkland that overlaps with DOS will continue to be parkland.

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: So just to note that all these protections very much still stay in place and are considered and analyzed if and when a home or any development is proposed.

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: Adjacent to or kind of within that buffer area by multiple agencies.

chapters.summary: Morano asks whether adding usable backyard or lot area could change assessed value or property taxes; Ferrara says DCP cannot answer independently but will consult resources and follow up.
chapters.title: Morano asks about assessed value and property tax impacts

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I also want to ask about the practical impact on homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: For a property where the correction effectively adds usable backyard or lot area back to the property, could that change the property's assessed value or property tax bill?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And if so, has anyone analyzed how significant that impact would be?

utterances.speaker: Catie Ferrara Iannitto
utterances.text: I don't know that we independently can answer that at this time, but we're happy to consult our resources and get back to you if an answer to that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilman, we're just going to ask you to wrap up your question.

chapters.summary: Morano asks what affected homeowners would face without corrections; Todorovic says Sites 1 and 2 could not be built, Site 3 could not be enlarged, and even after adoption CPC review would remain because DOS would still exist on the sites.
chapters.title: Morano asks practical consequences if mapping corrections are not made

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Okay, finally, finally.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If these mapping corrections were not made, what would the practical consequence be for the affected homeowners?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Would they continue to face restrictions or approval requirements based on boundaries that everyone now agrees are inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And more broadly, how does this amendment advance the original goals of the South Richmond zoning relief without weakening environmental protections that were intended to remain in place?

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: If retained, the homes would not be able to be enlarged or built.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Site number one, not built at all.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Site number two, not built at all.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Site number three, enlarged.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So they wouldn't be able to utilize their full property rights or development rights.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Site number one might need to go to the BSA.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: Site number two would need to do a complete orientation.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: And site number three, again, would be modest, but they wouldn't be allowed to do kitchen additions, enlargements in the rear yard to that extent.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: These sites, even if and when, or if this is approved, even if adopted, they still need...

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: City planning commission approval because there will still be DOS on the site, just less of it.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: So they will have flexibility again laterally to reorient their site, design their site.

utterances.speaker: George Todorovic
utterances.text: to a better extent for a more superior, sometimes we say, or a better site plan, but they will still need additional review, and the community board will get that review if and when that reoriented building footprint is proposed and developed.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you for your work on this.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Madam Chair, thank you for your patience.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis thanks Morano, asks if any committee members have questions, and excuses the applicant panel.
chapters.title: Chair Louis excuses South Richmond panel

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Do any members of the committee have questions for the applicants?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Seeing none, this panel is now excused.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much for being here today.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We appreciate your testimony.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks for public testimony, staff reports no one signed up, and after a last call she closes the public hearing and lays over the South Richmond items.
chapters.title: Chair Louis closes South Richmond public hearing and lays over items

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, are there any members of the public who wish to testify remotely or in person regarding this proposal?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: No, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We don't have anybody signed up online or in person.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If there are any members of the public who wish to testify regarding this proposal remotely, please press the raise hand button now.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Or if you are in person, please identify yourself to one of the sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This is the last call, 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Being that there are no members of the public who wish to testify regarding this, the pre-considered L.U.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Relating to the South Richmond Designated Open Space Tax Amendment, the public hearing is now closed and these items are now laid over.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis makes a closing statement on the Sojourner Truth–Mapes rezoning, says the developer did not adequately engage the union, and urges FEPS houses to commit to 32BJ for a fair contract covering existing and new properties.
chapters.title: Chair Louis raises labor concerns on Sojourner Truth–Mapes rezoning

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Before we conclude today, I just want to make a quick comment on the record regarding the Sojourner Truth MAPES rezoning that we voted on today.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I do want to uplift my colleagues wishes to support member deference and achieving the project at the requirements appropriate for his district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: However, it is clear that the developer has not adequately adequately.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: engaged with the union in developing this proposal.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And as a committee, we are left uncertain on what labor guarantees can be expected as a result of the new development being considered today.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The current commitment as presented was insufficient to ensure that workers will be prioritized in the new development with the new needs that the building will bring.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: As a council, our priority must be in supporting both our residents and the workers who are on the front lines every day, keeping our housing safe, maintained, and secured.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I strongly encourage FEPS houses to make a clear commitment to 32BJ to uphold a fair contract as

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: negotiations begin next year and to ensure that the needs of these workers are reflected in an expanded agreement covering both their existing properties and the new properties created through this rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Shulman says she echoes the Chair's sentiments, notes her district's developments have had resident, community, and 32BJ support, and says she voted for the project despite major concerns about union voice.
chapters.title: Council Member Shulman echoes labor concerns on Sojourner Truth–Mapes

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Yeah, I want to, I'm not going to repeat everything that Chair said, but I echo her sentiments.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Every development that I've had in my district has had the support of both the residents, the community, and 32BJ.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And the unions need to have a voice in this.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And there seems to have been some inconsistency in terms of the back and forth here.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So, but in terms of member deference, I did vote for the project, but I do have major concerns.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I wanted that on the record.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis thanks the public, colleagues, subcommittee, council staff, and sergeant at arms, and adjourns the hearing.
chapters.title: Chair Louis concludes business and adjourns meeting

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Showman.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That concludes today's business.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I would like to thank the members of the public, my colleagues, subcommittee, council, land use, and council staff, and the sergeant at arms for participating in today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This meeting is hereby adjourned.

summary: Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises voted on five land use proposals, approving all with modifications except Sojourner Truth–Mapes, which passed with one opposition.
Held public hearings on 108-05 68th Road, 100-12 Queens Boulevard, and the South Richmond designated open space text amendment, with applicant presentations, council Q&A, and public testimony.
Key themes included affordable housing, MIH options, member deference, labor concerns, Fontaine co-op impacts, small business displacement, and DOS mapping corrections.

topic: Zoning, Fort Hamilton Mews Rezoning, Brooklyn (C 260238 ZMK)
